name: OTHERLIVED SHELF EDITION: Experience Day Archive Club
description: A deliberately low-cost offshoot of the premium experience-day market, operating out of repurposed shipping containers and basement nodes on the Tier 1-2 boundary. Members pay a subscription to access a rotating library of recorded lived days — not celebrities or executives, but ordinary people: a night-shift water reclamation worker, a child's first day with a BCI implant, a Shelf vendor during a district lockdown. The recordings are raw, unedited, and donated voluntarily by contributors who receive small Quanta micropayments.
story_hooks: A routine archive session exposes the user to a recorded day that ends mid-action — the contributor appears to have been forcibly disconnected and hasn't been heard from since.
A Tier 4 sociologist is secretly paying Shelf contributors extra to record days in specific locations during specific windows, and no one knows why.
An entire week of archive content has been quietly replaced with subtly altered recordings — the same days, same people, but with certain events edited out.
